findings.issue: AC6 reject path is not tested. The approve and retry callback handlers each have dedicated tests (test_approve_callback_transitions_preview_to_publishing, test_retry_callback_links_regenerated_job); the [✗ Отклонить] branch does not. publish.py:376-389 transitions preview-sent → REJECTED and edits the preview to 'Отклонено. Бриф сохранён, можно повторить руками.' Regression in this branch (wrong target status, wrong edit text) would slip through.
findings.fix: Add test_reject_callback_transitions_preview_to_rejected mirroring the approve test, asserting the CAS to REJECTED and the edit_text payload.

findings.issue: AC2 (Kaneo/Symphony NOT engaged) has no unit/integration coverage. Architecture intentionally has zero code path from content-publisher to Symphony or Kaneo. Negative-existence ACs are hard to unit-prove without a structural test.
findings.fix: Optional: add a static-grep test asserting fabric/content-publisher/src/ contains no 'symphony', 'kaneo', 'workspace_manager' substrings. Or defer to Task 12/14 AVP.

findings.issue: AC4 user-facing half (the [🔄 Перегенерировать] inline button appears at low score and DOES NOT appear at high score) is not tested. test_preview_dispatch_sends_reply_and_clears_preview_pending uses score=72 (below min_score=80) but reply_markup is asserted reflexively (`reply_markup: bot.sent[0]['reply_markup']`). No high-score case verifies absence of the [🔄] button. A code change that flipped the conditional would not be caught.
findings.fix: Add two assertions: (1) low-score preview_dispatch → InlineKeyboardMarkup contains a button with callback_data starting with 'publish:retry:'; (2) high-score preview_dispatch → no such button. Use a parametrized score in [60, 90] and assert button presence/absence accordingly.

findings.issue: AC-T11 (HMAC rotation runbook in README) is asserted at decisions.md narrative level (Task 3 reports four runbooks), but no test statically verifies the README continues to ship the runbook with the current two-secret comma-separated format. A README rewrite that drops the runbook section would not be caught at test time.
findings.fix: Add a unit test that opens infrastructure/ansible/roles/content-publisher/README.md and asserts canonical markers exist: e.g. 'HMAC rotation' heading + the two-secret format 'CALLBACK_HMAC_SECRETS=<current>,<previous>'.

findings.issue: tech-spec Testing Strategy and Task 8 Verify-smoke name 'test_topic_filter.py' as a dedicated file. The substance of AC-T12 (3 negative dimensions + positive case) IS covered by tests inside test_publish_handlers.py after the Task 11 remediation pass. The file-naming gap is cosmetic — discoverability for future maintainers — but worth flagging because the spec author explicitly chose a separate file name. Not a coverage gap; not a regression risk.
findings.fix: Optional: move test_publish_topic_handler_rejects_wrong_chat_thread_or_user and test_publish_topic_handler_enqueues_matching_message into a new tests/test_topic_filter.py. Or update tech-spec Testing Strategy to acknowledge consolidation into test_publish_handlers.py.

findings.issue: Observation, not a regression. The four mock fixtures (mock_analyze_blog, mock_blogger_run_campaign_from_article, mock_mnemonic_mcp_stdio, mock_claude_subprocess) are defined as bare MagicMock() placeholders. Downstream tests rarely inject these fixtures — instead each builds its own ad-hoc _FakeProc / patch.object / monkeypatch tailored to the specific framing semantics (e.g. test_attest_envelope.py uses _FakeProc with stdin capture buffer + line-buffered stdout; test_analyze_gate.py uses a sync .communicate). This is by design (conftest placeholders cannot express stdin/stdout framing) but means the centralized fixtures earn very little. NOT mock drift — no duplicate logic found.
findings.fix: No action required. Optional future cleanup: either delete the unused conftest fixtures or convert them to parametrizable factories (e.g. mock_mnemonic_mcp_stdio(init_response, sign_response) -> FakeProc).

verdict_rationale: Verdict=`fail` per the strict rubric: any weak/missing AC fails the gate. AC2 (Kaneo not engaged — negative-existence), AC4 (no retry-button presence/absence assertion on bot side), AC6 (no reject-callback test) remain weak. Zero high findings, 4 medium, 1 low — the test layer is structurally sound; the remaining gaps are tightly scoped to two known callback branches (reject button + retry button presence-check) plus a structural negative-existence AC. Recommend pre-deploy QA proceeds with the three findings (F-001, F-003, F-004) opened as a targeted patch round on the bot tests.
